course:
The course topics are interesting, and one of a kind in UNAM. I definitely think this is a good course. However, I faced several challenges throughout the course. I think the flow of lectures was difficult to follow for someone with no background in electromagnetics or optics.  At times, advanced topics were discussed without sufficient background. The simulation-based assignments were both the strongest aspect of the course, as well as its weakest aspect. It was very challenging to translate my understanding of the course materials to matlab. It may be better to announce that some background in simulation is necessary for this course in the future.
Personally, I enjoyed solving the first two assignments. I studied the uploaded codes and learned how to simulate propagation, apply filters, and perform sampling. Even though the codes were very revealing, I personally learned from them as I had never done this before. However, for the next few assignments, I was at a loss on how to simulate certain things and often got confused by the questions. The assignments that I was able to solve were very satisfying. One last thing is that I definitely think that questions need to be clearer. It would be helpful

instructor: The instructor’s greatest strength is his very tolerant approach to helping in anything. In addition, it can be seen that he enjoys teaching the topic. He arranges both the content and the dates of the lessons, exams, and assignments to suit the students, which is very helpful for us.  All through the semester, he tried to tell us what hard work and learning really mean, rather than working for grades. He was really trying to see that his students were learning something. Although it was difficult for me to get used to this situation, thanks to him, I really understood what it means to study efficiently and learn about a subject. Coming to the weak points, the assumption of the class knowing MATLAB and has a background knowledge with electromagnetics or optics is perhaps the weakest point. Because the application of all the topics covered in the course to MATLAB was briefly shown and it was expected to learn it by yourself by researching it and spending a lot of your time, which can be difficult for a graduate student to learn it from scratch. Also, the slides provided for us to study were somewhat advanced. Outside of class, I had to spend a lot of time looking at the slides and reading the books, to understand what was being mentioned.

Course's strength is that it refers to unique subjects, which can help in the future of many of us. There are very interesting topics as well. Coming to the weak points, first of all, I believe that it is not a course for an average student. For a student with a background other than electromagnetic or optics, the topics of this course are not easy to understand. They are quite advanced with no given prerequisite. Thus, you need to spend almost 10 times more time on the topics covered in the lectures and study from the recommended books to understand them. This is also a very difficult situation for a graduate student who takes 2 more courses and does research along with it, because there is not that much time to spare. Another weak point of the course is that a student who does not know MATLAB or coding can have a hard time. Because, although some of the questions were theoretical, almost all of the scoring of the assignments and midterms are about how well you can code. Also, some of the questions were hard to grasp, and they could be clearer. In my experience, as a student who did not know MATLAB, it was quite difficult to code the concepts I learned in the course for assignments and midterm exams, and almost all my time in the semester was spent in this course. Therefore, the experience in MATLAB and medium-level optics knowledge can be announced as a prerequisite in the syllabus.
